source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) TRIZBench, Table 3, principle prediction (re-read for gap 3)
finding: Principle prediction in Table 3 is given the gold improve/worsen pair as input. Even with the pair, direct LLM prompting is below plain TF-IDF text retrieval and below the matrix lookup. Only reranking matrix candidates beats them.
numbers: Hit@3 case / patent: Matrix 0.67 / 0.48; TF-IDF 0.69 / 0.56; Qwen3-8B zero-shot 0.39 / 0.27; Qwen3-8B few-shot 0.51 / 0.25; Gemini-2.5-Pro zero-shot 0.45 / 0.31; few-shot 0.52 / 0.35; Qwen3-8B Matrix-Rerank 0.71 / 0.59; LLaMA3.1-8B Matrix-Rerank 0.68 / 0.55.
limits: Single run per cell, no confidence intervals. Hit@3 counts any one gold principle among the top 3. Gold sets can hold several principles, which makes the metric easier.
agent_relevance: A free-form pick-a-TRIZ-principle call is weak. Code-supplied candidates plus a model selector is the best arm measured. This supports the O4 design (code gives candidates, model selects) but only on label matching, not on answer correctness.

source: Computed chance baseline for TRIZBench Hit@3 (own calculation, no source reports one)
finding: TRIZBench reports no random baseline. If a case has k gold principles among 40 and the model lists 3 at random, the chance of at least one hit is 1 - C(40-k,3)/C(40,3).
numbers: k=1: 7.5%. k=2: 14.6%. k=3: 21.4%. k=4: 27.7%. Average gold-set size per instance was not read from the paper, so the true chance is somewhere in 7.5-28%.
limits: Hand calculation. Assumes uniform random lists and equal principle frequency. Real principle frequencies are skewed (a few principles dominate), so a frequency-prior baseline would score higher than uniform random.
agent_relevance: Every reported Hit@3 of 0.25-0.71 is above uniform chance, but a prior-frequency baseline is the fair floor and nobody has run it. Add it to any test of our own.

source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) TRIZBench, end-to-end pipelines (gap 3)
finding: When the model must predict the pair first and then the matrix gives principles, accuracy drops compared with giving the gold pair. The end-to-end route does not beat TF-IDF text retrieval.
numbers: Qwen3-8B ZS-Rerank (predicted pair, then matrix): Hit@3 0.59 case / 0.46 patent. LoRA-Rerank: 0.65 / 0.52. Gold-pair Matrix-Rerank (Qwen3-8B): 0.71 / 0.59. TF-IDF: 0.69 / 0.56. Patent pair Hit@3 (both parameters right in top 3): 0.13-0.28 across models.
limits: Whether TF-IDF sees the contradiction text is not stated in the passage I read. Pair prediction is only 0.29-0.45 PairF1 on cases, so the matrix path inherits a weak first step.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 is answered for patents and cases: end-to-end accuracy is about 0.46-0.59 for an 8B model, 10-12 points under the gold-pair version. If the pair is wrong the typed reframe is wrong, so O4 needs a check on the pair before the lookup.

source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) TRIZBench, Table 2, contradiction detection and pair recovery (gap 4)
finding: Detecting that a contradiction exists is much easier than naming the right pair. Prompts told models to abstain when no contradiction can be grounded, and detection F1 includes the abstention side. The paper does not report a separate false-alarm rate on trade-off-free text.
numbers: HasF1 (case detection) 0.75-0.87 for zero/few-shot LLMs, 0.82 PatentSBERTa retrieval, best 0.90 LoRA LLaMA3.1-8B. PairF1 (threshold 0.65) 0.29-0.45. Patent pair Hit@3 0.13-0.28.
limits: Cases come from TRIZ teaching material where every case has a contradiction by construction, so negatives are scarce. Detection F1 hides the false-positive rate. Single run.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays mostly open: no clean false-positive number. The 86/100 flag rate in Trapp and Warschat is the only direct figure. A trigger should be gated by a failing check, not by the model's own say-so.

source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) TRIZBench, grounding vs label accuracy (gap 10)
finding: Evidence quality and principle accuracy move together, and labels can be right with wrong evidence or wrong with right evidence. All data are patents and TRIZ cases.
numbers: Figure 3b: higher solution evidence F1 goes with higher principle Hit@3 (positive relation, no coefficient given). Example 1: athletic glove, pair right and Hit@3=1 but improving-aspect evidence missed. Example 2: vibrating alarm timepiece, improvement evidence F1=1.0 but pair wrong. PatentSBERTa evidence retrieval best (+0.14 F1 over modest TF-IDF gains).
limits: Evidence sets are built by retrieval over patent sentences, not by the model citing spans itself. Correlation only. Nothing tests final-answer correctness or any non-patent task.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open. A hint that span citation adds information beyond the label, never tested against answer correctness. Keep span citation as a cheap check, not a proven predictor.

source: Lee et al. (2026) TRIZ-inspired text-to-CAD, vanilla prompt arm (arXiv 2606.21378)
finding: The only paper found with a no-TRIZ prompt arm beside TRIZ prompts. A vanilla 'make a lighter chair' prompt cut more mass but hurt stiffness badly. Each TRIZ principle gave a smaller mass cut with less damage.
numbers: One chair, strength (#14) vs weight (#1), change vs baseline in mass / max stress / max displacement: vanilla -31.8% / +64.1% / +99.4%; TRIZ #1 segmentation -14.7% / -0.1% / +0.7%; #8 anti-weight -5.9% / +21.6% / +4.4%; #15 dynamics -4.0% / +33.2% / +16.3%; #40 composites -10.0% / +40.7% / +44.4%. Average TRIZ mass cut 8.7%.
limits: N=1 run per cell, no repeats. Prompts not token-matched: the TRIZ prompt adds baseline, contradiction and principle text. Column mapping from garbled PDF text, consistent with the paper's prose. No 'lighter but keep it stiff' free prompt, so it cannot separate principle content from merely naming the trade-off.
agent_relevance: Weak, direct hint that naming the trade-off plus a principle protects the other side of the contradiction. Gap 2 not closed: there is no restate-only arm. Treat as one anecdote.

source: Liu, Huang, Wang (2026) TRIZ-a, causal limits stated by the authors (arXiv 2610.04555)
finding: The authors say their traceable record does not show that TRIZ or the functional-information score caused the gain. They name an equal-budget unguided control as the missing test.
numbers: PowerDuck case: weighted-F1 0.9694 to 0.9982 with Local Quality (3) and Parameter Change (35) plus a train-only StandardScaler and LinearSVC.
quote: Traceability reconstructs the path, whereas causal attribution requires a matched-budget ablation
limits: Cybersecurity classification, not reasoning tasks. Paired reruns compare against baseline code, not against random or untyped mutation. The +0.15 to +4.23 F1 range was never put through an equal-budget test.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 is confirmed open and the source says so. Run typed vs untyped mutation at equal candidate count before crediting TRIZ.

source: Vargas-Hernandez, Schmidt, Okudan (2012) ASEE full text, tables re-read (gap 8)
finding: Full text of the conference version. The effect is small-sample and mixed: novelty is significant at two of three sites, quantity at none, and the authors call some results trends.
numbers: UTEP: 21 control, 9 TRIZ (senior mechanical engineering). UMD: 20 control, 21 TRIZ. Penn State also ran it. Quantity two-tail p-values 0.2879, 0.5409, 0.6291. Novelty p-values 0.0004, 0.0145, 0.5786. Quantity means in the text include 2.05 vs 3.80 and 4.10 vs 16.29 (column order garbled).
limits: PDF table text is scrambled, so the site-to-mean mapping is uncertain. The authors say some results miss p=0.05. Different warm-up and time limits per site. One task (LED traffic light snow). No Cohen d reported.
agent_relevance: Novelty and variety rise, quantity does not rise reliably. Matches K03. Effect sizes are not reported, so cannot be pooled.

source: Hernandez, Schmidt, Okudan (2013) J Mech Des 135(10), abstract via OpenAlex (gap 8)
finding: The journal version reports the same UTEP and UMD experiment as the 2012 paper, with Penn State only as an analysis partner. Same lab group, same traffic-light task. It is not an independent replication.
numbers: Two institutions ran it (UTEP, UMD). Metrics: quantity, novelty, variety. Conclusion: novelty and variety improve, quantity slightly lower. No effect sizes in the abstract. 85 citations (OpenAlex).
limits: Abstract only for the journal text. I found no independent-lab repeat and no non-engineering task in any source I could open.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 stays open. Do not count the 2012 and 2013 papers as two sources.

source: Dumas and Schmidt (2015) Relational reasoning as predictor for engineering ideation success using TRIZ, J Eng Des (gap 6)
finding: TRIZ raised novelty, and the size of the gain rose with the person's relational reasoning ability.
numbers: Abstract: TRIZ instruction significantly increased novelty; the gain was linked to relational reasoning score. Sample size, correlation and effect size not available (publisher page 403). 47 citations.
limits: Abstract only, from OpenAlex. No numbers.
agent_relevance: Suggests the reframe works through analogy mapping, so a weaker model may gain less. Test the typed reframe across model sizes. Gap 6 half answered for people, numbers missing.

source: Livotov, Chandra Sekaran, Masudah (2019) Lower abstraction level of TRIZ inventive principles improves ideation productivity, IFIP AICT (gap 6)
finding: Rewriting sub-principles in less abstract wording produced more ideas than the classical wording in a 10-minute exercise. Idea spread across MATCHEM-IBD fields also differed between wordings.
numbers: Three groups of undergraduate and graduate students (mechanical and process engineering), three design problems, 10 minutes, classical vs modified sub-principles. Counts and tests are not in the abstract.
limits: Abstract from the HAL metadata API. The full PDF sits behind a bot wall, which I did not bypass. Measures idea count, not novelty or correctness.
agent_relevance: Concrete wording of each principle likely matters. In a typed reframe store each principle with a one-line concrete example. Not yet tested on a model.

source: Springer IFIP TRIZ 2025 and 2026 chapters on LLMs (gap 7), metadata check via Crossref
finding: Titles confirmed, abstracts and numbers not retrievable. Chapters: Contradiction Processing Using LLMs and Generative AI (10.1007/978-3-032-08847-5_12); Investigating the Integration and Adaptation of ARIZ with LLMs (_22); Reframing TRIZ Tools as Cognitive Skills for AI-Assisted Inventive Problem Solving (10.1007/978-3-032-43196-7_9). Also Automated TRIZ Function Model Generation (_14), LLM-Based Functional Modeling (_16), Multi-agent Patent Drafting (_10), and AI for TRIZ: ChatGPT vs. Kangaroo (10.1007/978-3-662-70698-5_8).
numbers: OpenAlex citation counts: _12 has 4, _22 has 3, the 2026 cognitive-skills chapter has 0. No abstract text anywhere.
limits: Springer pages redirect to a login. Not opened. Cannot say whether any has a controlled comparison.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open. Do not cite these for numbers.

source: Chang, Chien, Yu, Chu, Chen (2016) Effect of TRIZ on the creativity of engineering students, Thinking Skills and Creativity (gap 8)
finding: Only metadata found. The abstract is withheld in Semantic Scholar and Crossref. 70 citations (OpenAlex).
limits: Not opened. Could be the nearest independent human check on the Hernandez result.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 stays open. Reading this paper is the cheapest next step for an independent human replication.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT, prompt-strategy comparison (arXiv 2408.05897), re-read for gaps 1 and 2
finding: Compared four prompt strategies inside the TRIZ pipeline on 34 cases with GPT-4. Every arm already uses TRIZ, so there is no no-TRIZ arm and no free-reframe arm.
numbers: 34 test cases (3 more used for few-shot). Step 4 solution reasoning: CoT plus few-shot cosine similarity M=0.824, SD=0.033. The authors chose plain few-shot because it matched scores with fewer input tokens. CoT plus few-shot was not additive.
limits: Metric is similarity to a reference solution, not expert correctness. Temperature 1 for step 4. No random-principle arm.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 2 remain unmeasured here. Small note for G7: the cheaper prompt tied the dearer one.

source: Szczepanik and Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents, re-read (arXiv 2506.18783)
finding: One gantry-crane case, judged by comparison with the published solution. The TRIZ specialist was left free to choose tools and often skipped its retrieval tool.
numbers: Recovered 1 of 2 published solutions; 150,000-250,000 tokens per run (from earlier file a14).
limits: No baseline arm, no single-call control, no raters.
agent_relevance: Adds nothing to gaps 1 or 2. Shows drift when the model decides whether to use the TRIZ table, so code should force the lookup.

finding: Section 8.4 compares TRIZ-only, Design Thinking-only, SCAMPER-only and the full pipeline in words only. No scores per arm.
numbers: No numbers for the single-method arms. The TRIZ claim scored InnovationScore 0.500 in the one case read.
limits: Qualitative. The score is the system's own graph score, not an external judge.
agent_relevance: No evidence on gap 1, 2 or 5. Do not use as a measure of TRIZ value.

source: Xu, Wu, Zhao (2026) TRIZ-RAGNER ablation, Table 3 (arXiv 2602.23656), re-read (contested source)
finding: The ablation removes retrieval, reranking and the structured prompt from a TRIZ entity-tagging system. None of the ablations swaps TRIZ-typed knowledge for untyped knowledge.
numbers: Full F1 84.2 (P 85.6, R 82.9). Without retrieval 78.1; without reranking 79.8; without structured prompt 76.6. Baselines: GPT zero-shot 73.7, GPT with prompt engineering 76.9. Text reports +7.3 points over the strongest baseline. 3 seeds.
limits: Critique flagged this preprint as contested: no model named, pasted-looking text. Patent entity tagging, not answer generation.
agent_relevance: Does not answer gap 9. The structured prompt gives the biggest single drop (7.6 points), a weak hint that slot format matters, from a contested source.

source: AutoTRIZ discussion citing Yilmaz et al. on randomly chosen design heuristics (arXiv 2403.13002)
finding: The AutoTRIZ authors repeat, second hand, that randomly selected design heuristics improved human design outcomes. If that holds for TRIZ stimuli, the choice of principle may matter less than having any structured prompt.
numbers: 77 heuristics drawn from over 3,000 design outcomes (Yilmaz et al.); randomly selected heuristics produced improved outcomes. No figures given in the AutoTRIZ text.
limits: Second-hand statement. The primary papers (their refs 76, 77) were not opened. Different method from TRIZ.
agent_relevance: Strengthens the need for a random-principle arm (gaps 2 and 9). If random works as well, only the forced restatement is paying.

source: Coverage check for ideal-final-result prompting studies (gap 5), Crossref listing 2023-2026
finding: Crossref searches for TRIZ plus LLM, and TRIZ plus ChatGPT experiments, returned AutoTRIZ, Nuclear TRIZ GPT, a Llama 2 patent-RAG matrix tool, the Springer IFIP chapters and student ChatGPT experiments. None isolates an ideal-final-result prompt.
numbers: About 50 titles scanned over two queries. Zero IFR-only LLM studies. Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and arXiv search rate-limited me and the WebSearch budget was spent, so coverage is partial.
limits: Absence in two keyword queries is weak evidence. Title-level matching only.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays open. IFR as a stand-alone prompt has never been measured, so keep it as an untested O8 candidate.
